**12.** (a) $0.5 \pm 2.58 \times 0.005 \to (0.487, 0.513)$: we are 99% confident that between 48.7% and 51.3% of season-ticket holders get their transfer news primarily from social media. (b) (i) False — the interval contains 50% (the point estimate *is* 50%), so there is no evidence that more than half do. (ii) False — the standard error measures the uncertainty of the estimate, not what share of the population was polled. (iii) False — reducing the standard error requires polling *more* season-ticket holders. (iv) False — a 90% confidence interval is *narrower* than a 99% interval.

**14.** (a) We are 95% confident that season-ticket holders watched a full match on 3.40 to 4.24 of the past 30 days, on average. (b) 95% of intervals constructed this way from repeated samples would capture the true population mean. (c) Wider. (d) Larger.

**16.** (a) A sampling distribution. (b) Right skewed — with $p = 0.13$ and $n = 40,$ the expected number of goals per sample is $40 \times 0.13 = 5.2 < 10,$ so the success-failure condition fails.
